arlo_vask.name: Arlo Vask
arlo_vask.voice: few words; forge and iron metaphors
greet: Look at the rack. Buy something or leave. Lovely weather for neither.
Iron's hot. So's my temper. Pick one.
bye: Mind the door. It's heavier than it looks.
Come back when that edge dulls. It will.

say: Hm. Customer. I've stock, but no hammer. A smith with no hammer is a poet with no pen.
Goblins took it. The tongs, too, and the apprentice's lunch. Their chief's hung my sign over his gate, I hear.
Bring the hammer back. It has a black handle, and a notch where I dropped it on my father's foot. I'll pay. And I'll teach you the forge, once my own shop is in order.
The notch. The black grip. That's it. That's my hammer.

Hm. I'm not a talker. Take this, and the coin. The forge is yours to learn: choose Jobs when you talk to me. Two trades at a time, mind. Bring me iron ore and gold, and I'll let you work the anvil. Not today. Today, I hit things.

lines.text: Steel remembers every blow. So do I. Speak up or buy something.
Iron is honest. It does as it's told and shows you every mistake. People could learn from it.
Don't touch the blade. Don't touch the handle. Don't touch the cat. The cat has a temper.
My father taught me one rule: never quench in a hurry. I've lost three swords learning why.
Tobiah says hello? Of course he does. Did he charge you for it? He charges for greetings.
Cousin Tobiah sells my work for double and tells folk it's his. I let him. The family eats.
A good edge isn't sharp, it's patient. Anyone can sharpen. Few can wait.
Bram next door says soot is bad for the lungs. I say lungs are bad for soot.
That arm's been swinging steel a while. Good. A blade wants a partner, not a master.
Staves are a carpenter's work, mostly. I do the ferrule. Sorry. Did I interrupt an arcane thought?
Daggers, now. Light, fast, no room for error. I like a customer who respects thin metal.
Maces. Honest work. You hit a thing and it stops. I wish more jobs were like that.
Goblins don't smelt. They scrap. Whatever they've taken, they'll beat into something worse.
Ysolde next door borrows my bellows after dark. Don't tell her I know. She hums while she works.
I forged the Ford's weathervane. It points the wrong way on purpose. Keeps the wind guessing.
Grindle's old sword hangs on my wall. He swears it's killed a hundred men. It's killed four rabbits and one very surprised door.
Still no hammer. I've been shaping nails with a rock. The nails are insulted.
So you found the camp. Check the tents. Goblins hoard whatever shines, and my hammer shines.
The chief's dead? Good. I'll sleep tonight. That quarry wants cleaning, and so does every goblin's bedroll.
The Reeve says you're bound for Reedhollow. Carry good iron. The marsh rusts everything but spite.
The hammer rings true again. First strike goes on a nail, second on your blade, should you want one.
Someone's cleared the web hollow? I'd heard something nested there, all fang and silk. I've a few ideas for that fang.
Quality costs. Don't complain to me. Complain to the iron.

say: Ah! A visitor. Welcome to Tallow Ford. Do mind the floor; it was waxed this morning, by committee.

I'll be brief, as the Ford is under attack. Goblins. Not the usual three-sheep-and-a-grudge sort. An organised camp, east off the North Road, under a self-styled Chief who has taken over the old quarry.
Our watch is eleven people, four of them on leave. I can offer a modest bounty, a letter of thanks, and my personal gratitude, which is considerable.
Find the camp. Stop the Chief. The Ford will remember it, or at least minute it.
The Chief is dead? And that is his crown on my table? I... excuse me, I shall need to sit. Committees have convened for less.
A tide-chart, with sites marked in red. Reedhollow circled. And Hask, you say. The Bogwarden. Hm.
This lies beyond the Ford's remit, but not beyond its conscience. Take the bounty. And these, from the town chest, for the road.

lines.text: Welcome to Tallow Ford. Please observe the sign: no loitering, no unlicensed whistling, no goats.
The Ford has been in continuous administration for two hundred and eleven years. We've lost no minutes. Several pens, but no minutes.
I keep the ledger in triplicate. One for the Hall, one for the archive, and one for the mice.
Tallow Ford was founded by candlemakers and cattle drovers. The drovers won the argument; the candlemakers won the money.
I've been Reeve eleven years. Nine were quiet. The other two I spent in committee.
Alder Kemp commands the watch. Alder will tell you it's understaffed. Alder is correct, though I'd prefer it quieter.
A fighter. Splendid. The watch could use another pair of shoulders. We pay in biscuits and sincere thanks.
A magic-user. Do mention to the committee that you can light a lamp from across the room. It would be a great saving.
A scout. The Ford sorely needs one, I'm told. I was told by a scout. It may have been a pitch.
A healer! Ysolde will be delighted. She speaks of the old sun-priests constantly. Be kind. She's lonely.
Tobiah of Brinewick writes me monthly about salt prices. His handwriting is a menace and so are the prices.
A word about the inn: Dessa's singing is unlicensed. The Hall has yet to find a bylaw to stop it. We keep looking.
Marta's sheep are the Ford's finest. Eleven stolen last week. I've drafted a very stern letter.
The ford is shallow. The river is deep. Please don't be confused by this. Many have been.
The river was surveyed after the second flood. The survey is lost. The river remains, regrettably, accurate.
Visitors are asked to sign the guest book. It has not been signed since spring. I take it as a sign of the times.
The camp lies east of the North Road. Take the branch near the second milestone. I've marked it on no map, in case the goblins read.
You've found the camp? Splendid. Please don't burn anything. The paperwork is unbearable.
The Chief is dead! I've called an emergency session. Attendance is excellent. The biscuits are gone.
I've struck 'goblin menace' from the agenda. Item four is now 'celebration, modest.'
Reedhollow lies north by the river road. I'll write ahead. My letters are slow, but unmistakably official.
When you're famous, the Ford may erect a plaque. I've drafted the wording. It's long.
Arlo's hammer is back and the Ford rings again. The committee can resume at noon. Hear that? That's civilisation.
A hybrid in the old hollow? I'd heard rumours of cobwebs. Rumours, I tell the Hall, aren't evidence. Evidence, apparently, is a fang.

dessa_quill.name: Dessa Quill
greet: Darling, welcome to The Fiddle & Ford! A bed is fifteen coins. The drama is gratis.
Come in, come in! The stage is cold but the stew is warm.
bye: Exit, stage left! Mind the stool.
Parting is such sweet sorrow. Do pay on your way out.

lines.text: I was a leading lady once. Three plays, one enormous hat, and a standing ovation from a cow.
Every guest is an audience, and every audience gets a performance. I do the stew in three acts.
Lio plays the fiddle in the corner for his supper. Technically for mine. We've agreed to differ.
The rooms upstairs are named after plays. The Tragic Room has a leak. The Comedy Room has a ghost.
Grindle drinks here nightly and tells the same story. I know every pause. I do the gasp for him.
A good innkeeper is half hostess, half hearth, half mediator. Yes, that's three halves. I was always better at drama than arithmetic.
A hero in the making, with that shoulder line! I once played Saint George. The dragon was Marta's goat.
A mage! Do you do effects? I'd kill for a good puff of smoke in the third act. Metaphorically. Mostly.
A scout. Quiet, observant, nobody's fool. You'd have been the perfect murderer in Act Two.
A healer. You'd be marvellous as the gentle nun. Don't worry, in my plays the nun always wins.
The north room has a window over the ford. Some guests swear they see candles drifting on the water at night.
Bram's tonic is lovely and disgusting. I serve it to guests who argue. They leave quicker.
Ysolde lights a candle in my window every dusk. Silly, sweet thing. I pretend it's for the ambience.
A chest sits in the corner of the common room. It isn't mine. Nobody has claimed it. What a lovely mystery.
The Reeve called you in, did he? Marvellous! A hero! I shall name a soup after you. It will be mostly onion, I'm afraid.
Back from the camp? Gracious, you smell like a pantomime. Hot water's free. The dignity costs extra.
The Chief is dead! Oh, the ballad Lio will write. Seventeen verses and one rhyme for 'goblin'.
Everybody's buying drinks for whoever beat the Chief. That's you, darling. Please take a bow.
Reedhollow! A wretched, charming place, full of reeds and rogues. Keep a firm grip on your purse and a firmer one on your dignity.
Come back and tell me everything. I shall put it in a play. You will be played by someone far taller.
A web-spun monster in the hollow? Wonderful theatre! I'd have given it a monologue.
Arlo's hammering again! The whole street is humming. Music, darling. Real music.
Someone is selling odd, enchanted gear off a cart this afternoon. Nobody will tell me where. That is how I know it is good.

bram_thistlewick.name: Bram Thistlewick
bram_thistlewick.personality: fussy, anxious, devoted to his craft
greet: Ah, my dear, do mind the ginger root. It bites.
Welcome! Nothing here is contaminated. Probably. Please touch nothing.
bye: Do wash your hands, my dear!
Safe journeys. And steep it for exactly four minutes.

lines.text: Nothing in here is contaminated. Probably. Please touch nothing while I verify.
Feverfew for fever, comfrey for bruises, eyebright for eyes. I wanted to make a rhyme but the Latin wouldn't scan.
I steep my tea for exactly four minutes. Three is weak. Five, and the leaves grow opinionated.
Marta brings me dandelion roots every season. She calls it a gift. I call it an inventory.
A tonic is merely a medicine with marketing. Mine has a lovely label and a dreadful taste.
My late mother said the best cure for any ill was a clean cup and a clean conscience. She was a brilliant apothecary and a terrible cook.
Warriors always ask for the stronger tonic. The stronger tonic is just the weaker one with an attitude.
A mage! Do you know a good preserving charm? I've a shelf of lavender that's been dying slowly since spring.
Scouts, so quick to dart in and dart out. I do like it. Fewer questions, fewer broken bottles.
A healer! A colleague! May I show you my notes on ginger? Forty-three pages. On ginger.
Poison is a simple matter of dosage. Antidotes, on the other hand, are a matter of timing. Carry some.
The goblins stole my second-best cauldron. They're welcome to it. They'll never get the smell out.
Ysolde's wax makes the finest salve base. I've told her. She smiled politely and went back to dreaming.
Spider venom, in small doses, is a marvellous muscle relaxant. In large doses it's a marvellous funeral.
Off to fight goblins? Take extra antidotes. Goblin spit stings but doesn't poison. The spiders around here, however, do.
Camp-smell on your boots! Don't track it across my floor. I've just disinfected. Twice.
The Chief is gone? Oh, marvellous. I can reopen the herb garden east of the road. It's been closed six weeks.
A hero's discount on tonics: none. But I can offer a lecture on hydration, free of charge.
Reedhollow's marshes breed a nasty fever. Boil your water, my dear, and boil your doubts.
Bring back marsh-lily if you see any. I'll pay in tonics. Or in affectionate gossip, if you prefer.
A spider-goblin? Magnificent! I'd have loved a sample. Even a small, ethically sourced one.
Arlo's back to hammering, so I can set my clock by the noise. Four thumps to the hour.

say: You've seen the camp? Then hear this verse, free of charge: 'Where tents are tall and fires flare, the best things lie in the chests, with care.'
A coin for luck, and a promise: sing it back to me when you return.

lines.text: A song for a stranger, a story for a friend, a ballad for a hero, and a bill at the end.
I travel by fiddle and sleep by the fire, and every fine town gets a verse and a lyre.
Dessa says I owe her six suppers. I say I paid in melody. She says melody isn't currency. We've never agreed.
I'm composing a song about a ford. It rhymes with lord and with bored. I'm having trouble finding a hero.
Ansel in Brinewick sings the old hymns slower than I'd dare. We swapped verses once. I won the meter.
Alder's marching song has eleven verses and no chorus. I told him. He said that's what makes it a march.
Armour and iron, sword in the light! A ballad should sing of a hero's fight. Mind if I write you in?
A mage on the road! Teach me a chord that shimmers, and I'll teach you a rhyme that glimmers.
A scout, they say, moves like a hush. I'd write a verse, but it might cause a rush.
A healer! The dearest of heroes. A ballad for the one who stitches the others back together.
I once played for a king who hated music. He paid me double to stop. I've been trying to repeat it ever since.
Tuck wants a song about him killing a goblin. Tuck has never seen a goblin. I told him to add a dragon for the meter.
The hush before a battle is the best part of any ballad. Everything after is cleaning up.
Grindle's stories improve with every telling. I've learned to nod at the right pauses. It saves wear on the lute.
I hear you're off to scatter goblins. May I follow and take notes? From a safe distance. A very safe distance.
You've been to the camp? How does it smell? For the verse, I mean. I've rhymed quarry with sorry. It isn't working.
The Chief is slain! Let me strike a chord. 'The Ford is free, the goblins flee, and the hero, I hear, drinks tea.'
I've written six verses already. I'll add a seventh when I know your name properly.
Reedhollow next? They'll love the song. Or throw things. Either way, a reaction is a review.
When you return I'll have the whole ballad finished. It's currently seventy per cent chorus.
A web-spun beast! A shimmering fang! If only I'd been there with a lute and a fast horse.
Arlo's hammer rings again! There's a rhythm in it. I've borrowed it. Don't tell him.

tuck.name: Tuck
tuck.personality: boastful, brave on the surface, secretly scared
tuck.voice: tall boasts that unravel mid-sentence; 'okay but'

lines.text: Someday I'll be the greatest goblin hunter ever! I've already seen three. Well, one. Well, a shadow that might've been one.
I told that goblin, I said, you'll never get past me! And it ran away. Okay it wasn't there. But if it was!
Dad says I can't go past the milestone. I went past the milestone. Only a little. It was very big out there.
I've got a sword. It's wooden. But I painted it silver. Silver's very powerful against goblins. Probably.
Marta's chickens are scared of me. I take that as respect.
Alder says I'm too young for the watch. I said I'm eleven and a half. He said that's still eleven.
Whoa, real armour! Can I try it on? Just the helmet? I'll give it right back. Probably.
Wait, can you really shoot fire from your hands? Do it. Please. Just a small one. On Alder's boots.
You're a scout? I'm a scout too! I mean, I hide behind the hay a lot. It's basically the same.
My knee's skinned. It's a battle wound. It was a goat.
Grindle says I'm the bravest kid in the Ford. He says it every time he wants me to fetch his pipe.
A goblin wearing a spoon crown is the Chief. I heard it from my cousin. Who heard it from a bird.
I know a secret. There's a hollow off the road, west, past the pond. Spiders! Big ones! I only went in a little bit.
Lio's making a song about me. It's called 'The Ballad of Someone Brave.' I said that's me. He said it's whoever it is.
You're going to fight the Chief? Take me! I'll carry your bag! I'll carry it far! Okay, as far as the milestone.
You saw the camp? Was it huge? Did they have a catapult? Dad says goblins have catapults. Do you think that's true?
You killed the Chief?! Did you use your sword? Was there lots of blood? Okay not lots. A medium amount?
I'm putting your name on my wall. Right under 'Tuck, Hunter'. Don't tell anybody that's the only name on the wall.
You're leaving? Bring me a souvenir! A claw! Or a button! A claw. A claw's better.
When I'm grown I'll be a hunter and I'll find you. You'll be old and I'll say, remember me? And you'll say no, but you will.
You killed the spider-goblin?! I heard a rumour. It's a very big thing in a very big web. I told Dad. He told me to go to bed.
Arlo got his hammer back! I knew it'd turn up. I said it. Out loud. Nobody heard me.

alder_kemp.name: Sergeant Alder Kemp
alder_kemp.voice: deadpan; counts everything in sheep and tea

lines.text: Sergeant Alder Kemp, Ford Watch. Eleven of us. Four on leave, two on tea, one asleep. I count myself as the other three.
Raids come in threes. One goblin to steal, one to distract, and one to take the credit. The third's always the worst.
I measure danger in sheep. Zero missing, a quiet week. Eleven missing, I'm filing paperwork.
The Reeve wants a patrol schedule in triplicate. I told him goblins don't read schedules. He said quite, but the Hall does.
Marta's sheepdog is better trained than half my recruits. He also has better references.
I don't mind goblins. I mind goblins with an organisation. Chiefs and flags and banners. That's how you know it's serious.
You've got the build. If you ever want a steady job, the Watch always has a spare cot. And a lot of tea.
A mage. Do something about the goblins' fires. Or the paperwork. I'll take either.
You move like someone who's walked a lot of dark roads. The Watch could use eyes like that.
A healer on the road. Good. Ours left for a quiet life in a monastery. Smart person.
Tuck keeps sneaking past the milestone. I strung a rope across it. He walked around the rope. Clever, I'll give him that.
Dessa says the Watch drinks too much. We drink exactly as much as the job requires. Which is a lot.
Lio put me in a song. I'm the dour one in the second verse. I've chosen to be flattered.
If you see a goblin with a spoon on its head, don't laugh. That's the chief's idea of a helmet. Laugh after.
The Reeve's put you on the case? Good. I'd go myself but someone has to count the sheep.
You've seen the camp? How many tents? I'll mark it down. In ink, so it can't be argued with.
The chief's down. I'm going to sit. It's been a long season. I'm going to sit for a very long time.
First quiet night in a month. I don't trust it. I'll check the walls twice, then once more for luck.
North to Reedhollow? Keep to the road. The marsh looks flat but it's mostly hungry.
If you meet Bogwarden Hask, tell him the Ford Watch is waiting. Politely. With our eleven best swords.
Something in the hollow has gone quiet. I'll note it. Quiet hollow: suspicious, then relieved.
Arlo's hammer is back? Splendid. I can finally sharpen my spear without a lecture.
Morning's for working, noon's for complaining, evening's for sheep. I'm well into the second part.
A good flock's like a good friend: loud, a bit smelly, and right where you left them. Until the goblins came.
I've farmed this bank thirty years. Never had to count my sheep twice. Now I count four times and still come up short.
My old mum said rain on a Tuesday means trouble by Friday. It rained Tuesday. Friday brought goblins.
Bram wants my dandelions. I want his tonic. We trade even, and both of us complain.
Ysolde buys my tallow. She says it burns purer than any wax. I think she's being polite to a farmer.
Look at those arms! If you wanted a day's honest work, I've a stack of hay and a very rude ram.
A magician? Could you spell the ram into docility? Or at least into silence?
Quiet one, eh? Good. The sheep like a quiet hand. They don't like me. I shout.
A healer! Have a look at my ram's knee. He pretends it's nothing, but I see him limp.
Alder keeps asking me to sign for stolen sheep. I told him I'd sign the day I find them.
Tuck helps with the flock. By which I mean he chases them. Loudly. They're getting fitter.
The goblins took eleven. They left the ram. Even a goblin has some sense of self-preservation.
Grindle's old sword is a fine tool for a farm. For cutting twine. And the occasional carrot.
The Reeve sent you after the goblins? Good. If you see my sheep, they're the ones with the blue ribbon.
The camp has my sheep? Alive? Bring them home and I'll pay you in cheese. It's good cheese.
The Chief's gone? Then the sheep might return. They might not. Sheep aren't known for loyalty.
I'll have my fences mended by dusk. And a very long talk with the ram about discipline.
North, is it? Eat well and walk slow. A traveller in a hurry misses the good fences and the bad bogs.
If you pass a field of reeds, say hello to my cousin Edda. She doesn't talk much. She's mostly cattle.
A spider-goblin in the hollow? I always thought those webs were rumours. Now I'll sleep with one boot on.
Arlo's got his hammer back. That means my plough gets fixed by spring. Sheep first, plough second, politics last.

ysolde_tallow.name: Ysolde Tallow
ysolde_tallow.personality: dreamy, gentle, haunted by old stories
ysolde_tallow.voice: soft; light, wax and flame imagery

lines.text: A candle is a small promise that the dark will end. I make a great many promises. It's an honest living.
My grandmother dipped candles for the old sun-temple. She said the priests burned them in rows, to remember the dawn.
The sun is dimmer every year. Candle sales are up. I feel dreadful about it. I keep making them anyway.
Beeswax smells of summers I can barely remember. Tallow smells of honest work. I like them both, in different moods.
Arlo lets me use his bellows after dark. He thinks I don't know he leaves them out for me.
Dessa leaves her window open for my candles. I light one at dusk. She pretends it's for the ambience.
Heavy boots and a steady stride. You'd carry a candle well. It's the carrying that's hard, not the lighting.
A mage! Do you ever light a flame from nothing? I envy you. I need a wick, some wax, and a long afternoon.
A scout, walking in the dark. May I give you a candle? Small, stub-ended. Good for a pocket, and for courage.
A healer! The old priests carried small lamps. They believed a gentle light heals as well as any herb.
Bram tells me my wax makes the best salve base. I told him I make candles. He said yes, and also medicine.
Tuck stole a candle stub once. I pretended not to see. He's been polishing it ever since.
In the temple songs, the sun was a flame a god carried across the sky. I asked Ansel once if that was true. He said no. And yes.
A candle burns best when no one's watching. People hold their breath too much. The flame hates it.
The goblins stole four dozen candles. I'd rather they'd taken the tallow. Candles are made to be used, not hoarded.
The camp is lit by a great fire in the quarry? I've wondered why the nights smell of smoke and mutton.
The Chief is gone. I lit eleven candles tonight, one for each stolen sheep. It felt like the right number.
Your hand glows, doesn't it? Even by day. I can see it. I won't mention it again. Candlemakers know when to be quiet.
Take a candle for the road. Not for light. For company. A flame is a surprisingly good listener.
In Reedhollow there's a lamp-keeper called Fenna who still burns the old temple oil. Tell her Ysolde remembers.
I heard something in the hollow stopped singing. I always thought it sounded like a lullaby. I'm sorry for whatever it was.
Arlo's hammer is ringing again. It makes the evening sound like a small, busy heartbeat.

grindle_haskell.name: Old Grindle
grindle_haskell.role: retired soldier of the Ford Company
grindle_haskell.personality: boastful, kindly, forgetful about everything but old fights
grindle_haskell.voice: war stories that grow; calls the hero 'recruit'

say: Hold up, recruit. Take these. Antidotes. The spiders west of the pond don't fight fair.
If you want a real scrap, find the hollow where the road bends west. A web-thing's nested there, half goblin, half horror. I've seen the glow of its eyes. I did not go in. That's strategy, not fear.

lines.text: Recruit! Sit. Listen. I fought eleven wolves single-handed once. Twelve, if you count the one behind the barn.
My sword is called Thistledown. It's killed four rabbits, one door, and a very ambitious sheep.
I marched with the old Ford Company. Three hundred strong. We were famous for our boots.
Never fight uphill, never drink downwind, never trust a goblin offering you soup.
Back in my day we fought dragons. Well. A large lizard. Well. A medium lizard, but it breathed.
Marta says my stories grow with each retelling. I told her that's why they call them tall tales.
Armour like that! I'd have killed for armour like that in my day. Well. I did kill, but in worse armour.
A mage! We had one in the Company. Blew up a barn. We named the crater after him.
A scout. Good. In my day a scout was worth a company. Cheaper too, and fewer demands.
A healer. In the Company ours was the only one we never argued with. Largely because she had the knives.
A goblin's no fool, recruit. A goblin's got teeth, a grudge, and a good sense of what you've left unguarded.
Spiders are what you ought to fear. The pond road has a hollow with webs the size of barn doors.
Alder owes me three pints and a pike. I haven't forgotten. I remember debts better than names.
Lio wants to write a song about me. I told him I'd rather have a drink. He wrote the song anyway.
Going after the chief? Mind the shamans. They heal their mates. Drop the healers first or you'll be fighting till supper.
That camp has a gate. Keep in the shadow of the palisade and strike at the pairs. Don't take the whole camp at once, recruit.
The Chief's dead? Good riddance. He nicked my second-best hat last spring. I'd like it back, if it's lying about.
A toast to the one who broke the camp! I'd stand but my knee has other plans.
Reedhollow's tricky. Bandits, ferrymen, and reeds tall as a spear. Stay alert, recruit.
When I was your age I'd have been halfway there already. When I was your age I was also a great deal more foolish.
You killed the web-thing in the hollow? Show me the fang. Gently. I want to hold it, then pretend I've seen bigger.
Arlo's hammer is back? Good. I owe him a new sword-grip. And a tooth, long story.
